question.text: What is STT (Securities Transaction Tax) and which derivative transactions attract STT?

answer.text: STT is a tax on securities transactions on Indian exchanges — it applies to equity F&O (sale of futures and exercise/sale of options) but NOT to currency or interest rate derivatives
STT applies to all derivative transactions including currency, interest rate, and equity
STT applies only to delivery-based equity transactions, not to any derivatives
STT is a tax collected by RBI on all forex transactions including currency derivatives

explanation.text: The Logic: STT applies to transactions in securities on recognized stock exchanges. For equity derivatives, STT is 0.02% on sale of futures (payable by the seller) and 0.125% on the sale of options on exercise (payable by the purchaser, on settlement price). STT does not apply to ETCD (currency derivatives) or ETIRD (interest rate derivatives). The Trap: CTT belongs to the commodity derivatives regime, not currency derivatives. STT does not apply to currency or interest rate derivatives. Note: The equity option exercise STT is 0.125% payable by the purchaser, not 0.10%; ETCD and ETIRD transactions do not attract STT.
